text.p: British publisher Dorling & Kindersley Holdings Plc said on Tuesday it expected full-year profits to be below the previous year.

Dorling said in a statement difficult conditions in the U.S. retail market and adverse currency movements had continued into the second half of the current year. Also, its decision to accelerate the growth of DK Family Learning would impact profitability in the short term.

"We do not expect the current strength in the British market to be sufficient to offset these effects and believe that profits for the year wil be lower than those achieved last year," chief executive Peter Kindersley said.
Kindersley said the company remained confident in its strategy for long-term growth.
Dorling said on Tuesday pretax profit rose 8.8 percent in the six months to December 31, 1996, to 6.775 million stg on turnover of 88.44 million.
U.S. turnover rose 7.7 percent to 36 million stg and British sales were up 16.8 percent at 27.2 million. Multimedia sales grew 31.4 percent to 13.1 million stg.
